dims.name: Acts
dims.question: What does the agent do on its own?

next_unlock.needs: Public evidence that the agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only.
Public evidence that there is a published protocol or communication layer between agents.
Public evidence that high-impact actions need a person's approval.
Public evidence that test or evaluation results are published.

gamma_ray.fact_ray: 23 facts: 23 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.
gamma_ray.built_from: Spinnable's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)

configs.what: Spinnable AI employees (called AI workers in the documentation) with its documented defaults.
Two or more workers in the same team or workspace, so one can delegate tasks to another.
A tool connection set to Read: workers using it can search and look up but not create, change or send.

facts.label: It executes actions itself
facts.fact: The documentation states workers act in connected tools, such as updating databases and sending emails.
facts.quote: They can check your calendar, update databases, and send emails.

facts.label: The agent handles routine tasks; the person is consulted on exceptions
facts.fact: The home page FAQ states that a worker schedules tasks, sends follow-ups and completes workflows without being prompted each time, that it will not take actions with external consequences without the person's approval and asks when unsure; no documentation page describes how that approval is configured.
facts.quote: it won't take actions with external consequences without your approval

facts.label: It works across several domains or systems
facts.fact: Workers connect to many tools across a business, from email and calendar to GitHub, Notion and Salesforce.
facts.quote: connect to 35+ tools to work across your entire tech stack

facts.label: It connects to external tools or services across a trust boundary
facts.fact: Each tool is connected by authenticating with the outside service through OAuth or an API key.
facts.quote: Authenticate with the service (OAuth or API key)

facts.label: A limit on it is a rule in prose
facts.fact: Persistent rules for a worker are written in prose in its Worker Policy.
facts.quote: Worker Policy instructions are treated as the highest-priority rules and apply across all conversations.

facts.label: Its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it
facts.fact: The troubleshooting page documents failure cases, such as a worker stopping mid-workflow, with causes and fixes.
facts.quote: Your worker initiates a task or multi-step workflow, but stops mid-way

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The privacy policy lists what the agents access: email, calendar, documents, messages and data from connected platforms.
facts.quote: When our AI agents work for you, they access:

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Spinnable's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.

items.title: Check and claim the GAMMA-Ray card
items.text: The card is beta and read only from public pages; Spinnable has not reviewed it. A correction is dated and published, and a file at /.well-known/fact-ray.json on their own domain raises the trust of every fact on it.

items.title: Measure one deployment
items.text: Pick one agent in one deployment; RiskMandate records its mandate, its grant and the gap, read-only. The lens page explains the measurement.

items.title: Run one of their agents under a harness, on stage
items.text: The same task run bare and under one policy, with the probes and the record public, as in our own harness runs (simulated data only).
